script: He didn't believe that I would do anything when I found out he was cheating.. For over a decade I was with a man that absolutely did not deserve my loyalty. Three days ago I walked in, eyes on him, and told him I already knew he was cheating—flushed with the proof I'd gathered. He admitted it, and I paused, like, "This wasn't your first time." He dropped his head, the way a kid drops a phone. "This… d‑bag" he muttered, "was never loyal to me since day one." He was awful, I was loyal, and I was pissed. But here's the thing. I opened Facebook and wrote a full post, detailing every lie, manipulation, abuse, and the cheating I'd pieced together. I added that I'd informed every husband, boyfriend, and friend of his that I know for sure he sleeps with their girl. So he has to worry about them and the entire area knowing him. It wasn't spreading as fast as I'd hoped. I started this to warn other women more than anything else. He is evil in a way I never imagined. Nobody was off limits to him— not even his own brother's girlfriend. Yeah, that's bad. I wasn't very familiar with the options, so I ended up on a screen with some kind of form. Then it hit me—turning a post into an ad for just $6, and Facebook would run it for three days to a targeted group that usually interacts with ads. Don't take kindness and loyalty as weakness.
